title: Does Kaiser Cover Doulas in California? 2026 Guide
body_markdown:
# **Does Kaiser Cover Doulas in California? 2026 Guide**


Yes. Most Kaiser members in California have coverage for doula care, and most Loula patients pay $0 out of pocket. You don't need a referral to get started, and you get to choose your own doula.


There is one important exception: self-funded Kaiser plans. Coverage for doula care can vary under these plans, and Loula does not currently work with self-funded Kaiser plans.


Here's what you need to know about using your Kaiser doula benefit in 2026.


### **The short version**


If you have Kaiser in California, doula care is covered under most plans.


Kaiser Medi-Cal and standard Kaiser commercial plans include coverage for doula care during pregnancy, birth, and postpartum. Most Loula patients pay $0 out of pocket.


The exception is self-funded Kaiser plans. Some self-funded plans may include doula coverage, but it isn't guaranteed and benefits can vary. Loula does not currently work with self-funded Kaiser plans, so if you have one, you'll need to check directly with Kaiser to understand your coverage.


### **What does a doula actually do?**


A doula provides nonmedical support before, during, and after birth. They can help you understand your options, prepare for labor, support you physically and emotionally during birth, and be there as you recover and adjust postpartum.


Unlike your doctor or midwife, your doula's focus is consistent, one-on-one support for you. Think of it as having someone in your corner who knows how this works and whose focus is you.


### **Why does Kaiser cover doula care?**


Research has linked doula support with better maternal health outcomes. One recent study of Medicaid enrollees found a 47% lower risk of delivering by C-section and a 29% lower risk of preterm birth among people with doula support.


California has also expanded access to doula care in recent years, including adding doula services as a Medi-Cal benefit in 2023.


### **What's covered?**


For most Kaiser members in California, covered doula care includes:


- One initial visit
- Up to eight additional visits that can be used before or after birth
- Support throughout labor and delivery
- Up to two extended three-hour postpartum visits
- Support through pregnancy loss, including miscarriage, stillbirth, and abortion


Additional postpartum visits may also be covered with a provider's recommendation.


Self-funded Kaiser plans work differently. Coverage under these plans can vary, so you'll need to check your specific benefits directly with Kaiser.


As of 2026, Kaiser members generally need to work with a Kaiser-contracted doula for their care to be covered. Loula can help you find a doula who works with your Kaiser plan.


### **What's not covered?**


Insurance covers eligible doula support, but some additional services doulas may offer aren't part of the covered benefit.


Services like massage, birth photography, placenta encapsulation, and belly binding generally aren't covered. Some doulas offer these services separately if you're interested in them.


### **Do you need a referral?**


No. You don't need a referral from your Kaiser doctor to start working with a doula.


Kaiser members are covered by a statewide standing recommendation for doula services, so you don't need to get a separate recommendation before getting started. Additional postpartum visits beyond the standard benefit may require a provider's recommendation.


### **What will it cost you?**


For most Loula patients, $0 out of pocket.


Most Loula patients with Kaiser pay nothing out of pocket for covered doula care.


Self-funded plans are the exception. Coverage and costs can vary depending on the specific plan, and Loula does not currently accept self-funded Kaiser plans.


Loula verifies your coverage before care begins, so you'll know what's covered before getting started.


### **How do you find a doula who takes Kaiser?**


Finding a doula who takes your Kaiser coverage shouldn't become another thing you have to figure out.


Loula works with more than 500 trained, vetted doulas across California. We verify your coverage, help you find someone who fits what matters to you, and handle the insurance and billing along the way.


For Kaiser members, we'll also make sure you're matched with a doula who can work with your specific plan. And if the fit isn't right, you can switch doulas at any time.


[Check your coverage](https://joinloula.com/connect) and find a doula who feels right for you.


### **Frequently asked questions**


**Does Kaiser cover doulas in California?**


Yes. Most Kaiser members in California have coverage for doula care, and most Loula patients pay $0 out of pocket. Coverage under self-funded Kaiser plans can vary, and Loula does not currently accept self-funded plans.


**Is there a copay for a Kaiser doula?**


Most Loula patients with Kaiser pay $0 out of pocket for covered doula care. Self-funded plans can work differently, so coverage and costs should be confirmed directly with Kaiser.


**Do you need a referral for a doula with Kaiser?**


No. You don't need a referral to get started. Kaiser members are covered by a statewide standing recommendation for doula services.


**How many doula visits does Kaiser cover?**


For most Kaiser members, coverage includes an initial visit, up to eight additional prenatal or postpartum visits, labor and delivery support, and two extended postpartum visits. Additional postpartum visits may be covered with a provider's recommendation. Self-funded plan benefits can vary.


**Does Kaiser cover a doula for miscarriage or pregnancy loss?**


Yes. Covered doula care can include support through miscarriage, stillbirth, and abortion.


**Can you pick your own doula with Kaiser?**


Yes. You can choose your own doula as long as they meet the requirements of your Kaiser plan. Loula can help you find a Kaiser-contracted doula who's available around your due date and fits what matters to you.
